name: get_close_all_blocked_message
doc:
Build the explanation CDKey for a blocked "Close all" action.

Sibling of [`Self::get_close_all_message`] and deliberately the same
shape: Rust owns the key, Native keeps only the toast render. FR-10
requires every Rust-produced row title AND disabled reason to travel as a
`DisplayString`/CDKey rather than a Rust bare string, and TC-20 guards it;
routing this round's new reason through a typed enum with the copy owned
in Kotlin would have left it as the one piece of Rust-decided
user-visible text that never enters the DisplayString pipeline.

TOTAL over [`OKTBatchCloseBlockedReason`] on purpose — no `_` catch-all,
so a future variant cannot silently fall through to someone else's copy.
`None` resolves to `Placeholder` (`DEFAULT_VALUE_NONE`): nothing is
blocked, so there is no message to show.

The two already-shipped reasons are mapped here as well, even though
Kotlin deliberately KEEPS its existing `when` branches for them
(`PureMainPositionsFragment.kt:775-787`, which resolve
`pr_trade_positions_toast_closeall_not_available` and
`pr_trade_positions_toast_close_all_disabled` directly). This round does
not re-route shipped text paths; the arms exist so the function is
genuinely total and so a later consolidation has nothing left to add.
They are intentional coverage, not dead code.

`SymbolDomainFilterActive` resolves to the platform-published key of
the asset class that is actually filtering
(`pr_trade_errormsg_alert_closeall_nosupport_cryptosymbols` /
`..._tradfisymbols`). Neither is a reuse of a shipped key: the shipped
copy names *Current instrument* and the options/voucher copy names a
product limitation, so both carry a different meaning (FR-7). The domain
is the EFFECTIVE one the list is filtered by, read from the Manager, so
the signature stays unchanged for both hosts.

name: reset_after_order
doc:
Post-order-success reset — native `TPSLViewBinder.clearTPSLConfig(false)`
parity. Native's `resetData` keeps the master take-profit/stop-loss
checkbox + panel visibility, and `clearInputLayout` is type-gated

ByRate / ByProfit leg keeps its value. Unlike [`Self::clear_all_tpsl`]
(uncheck / order-type switch — a full wipe to ByPrice), this leaves the
panel checked with the simple by-rate value intact after placing an order.
- advanced / OCO / MULTI / Trailing active -> clear the active advanced
config, then restore a parked simple ByRate / ByProfit draft when one
exists. Programmatic advanced presets without a draft return blank.
- inline simple -> per-leg: a ByPrice leg fully clears; a non-ByPrice
(ByRate / ByProfit) leg keeps its rate / profit value + strategy kind.
The master checkbox is Kotlin-owned (kernel does not drive it), so the host
simply does NOT uncheck it around this call. Host-synced context pricing
(entry / lever / position_size) is kept either way.

`&&`s two Rust state fields on the Kotlin side):
suppress = `is_new_coin_online_blocking` (`isNewCoinOnLineAndNotWhiter`,:3574)
|| `is_in_new_coin_countdown`    (`newCoinOnLineLv` true,:3576)
REQUEST 2 (Image 20): input ① now reads the Rust self-derived
`is_new_coin_online_blocking` (session-projected) instead of the
deprecated Native-push `is_new_coin_disabled` — iOS stopped pushing the
latter, so any reader still on it got `false` and the float-window was
never suppressed. `is_in_new_coin_countdown` is kept as-is.
When `true`, the (later-round) min-order-amount soft-keyboard float
window must be unbound / not bound; when `false`, it binds with the
min-size hint. The float-window widget that consumes this is a follow-up
round; this round delivers the predicate + its two inputs.

name: update_seekbar
doc:
**Seekbar percent selection** — BUG-5 (real-device 2026-06-03): selecting
a seekbar percentage did NOT fill the amount input because the trigger
panel had no percent action (the foundations note above predates the
seekbar attach). Wire the percent→amount chain mirroring the sibling
SpotLimit `update_seekbar` (`spot_limit_interactor.rs:665` decl + `:4513`
impl): `is_selected=true` writes `amount` from `percent × max-amount`
(rounded via the shared `calculate::percent_to_amount`) + records
`seekbar_percent`; `is_selected=false` clears both.

VALUE contract = trigger V1 NATIVE (`AbsSpotTradePanelPresenter`
`getSumMaxSize`/`getSumAvailable` :1036-1076): the max-amount the percent
scales is the side-aware balance — BUY → `max_size` (=`avail_eq`, the
base-ccy max-buyable), SELL → `available` (=`avail_balance`, the base-ccy
sellable) — with the loan portion subtracted when `!can_borrow` (V1 `if
(!canBorrow()) max = max.subS(loanMaxSize)` / `avi.subS(loanAvailable)`).
This is the SAME side-pick + loan-fold `on_depth_amount_clicked` /
`recompute_avail_displays_internal` use, so the seekbar amount matches the
displayed max-buy/max-sell figure. A2/H-1 — the multiply/divide/round is Rust
Decimal, never Kotlin.

name: sl_trigger_ratio_for_liq_check
doc:
Dynamic-trigger-price companion of [`Self::sl_trigger_px_for_liq_check`].

A ByDynamicPrice stop-loss leg emits `sl_trigger_ratio` and CLEARS
`sl_trigger_px` (the API rejects both -- see the OCO builder in
`base/make_order.rs`), so the static getter above returns "" for it. Native then
derives the comparison price from the ratio, but ONLY on panels whose
`supportTpslDynamicTriggerPx()` is true -- limit
(`FutureLimitTradePanelPresenter`:1646) and market
(`FutureMarketTradePanelPresenter`:602). Advanced-limit and SwapAdvanced do NOT
override it, so they must keep skipping the ratio path. The panel interactor owns
that decision plus the order price, so this getter only surfaces the raw ratio.

MULTI carries no dynamic stop-loss (`OKTMultiAttachParam` has no ratio field, and
`tpsl_multi_interactor::convert_params` drops it), hence "" while MULTI owns the
attach.

order sz). The editor anchors the estimated-PnL on entry+size; for the fixed-quantity close the

doc:
V2 state for `PureModifyContractAlgoOrderInteractor` (V1
`ModifyContractAlgoOrderFragment`, 686 LOC).

Contract-algo (TPSL) orders carry up to two legs (TP / SL) like the
spot-algo state, PLUS the contract identity triple
(`pos_side` / `td_mode` / `leverage`) the contract amend flow needs
to surface on the V1 dialog.  V1 also tracks the all-position-close
boolean which drives whether `new_size` should be sent over the wire
at all (V1 `amendOrder()` body: `if (isAllPositionClose) newSz = ""`).

24 fields total:
1. Identity (8)  — algo_id / order_id / inst_id / inst_type / order_type
+ pos_side / td_mode / leverage
1b. Display (3)  — side / tgt_ccy + immutable amount_snapshot
2. Inputs (8)    — TP triple + SL triple + size pair
3. Contract-specific (1) — is_all_position_close
4. Submit (5)    — submit_state + data_changed + is_reduce_only +
is_dirty + is_close

INDEX selection.

other `update_*` setters' partial-update convention). No-op after

here is enough to re-anchor the displayed percent — the binder calls
`compute()` after `setTriggerPxType` (V1 `setTp/SlMarketListener {
updateMarketInfo }`), and `apply_by_price_rate_linkage` now resolves the
per-leg anchor against the newly-selected base price (MARK / INDEX /
LAST) via `PriceSourceHost`. SPOT is unaffected (no mark / index data,
no type picker).

name: on_resume
doc:
V1 `onResume` — host signals panel visible.

Root-cause fix (R-MIG-216): the panel is a child of the main trade
session, so the instrument must be sourced FROM the session — it is not
pushed in. Previously `on_resume` only flipped the lifecycle flags and
never read the session instrument, leaving `state.instrument` empty
(`instId`/`baseCcy`/`quoteCcy`/`tickSz`/`lotSz`/`minSz` all blank) so
`fetch_max_available` failed with "inst_id is required" and the Kotlin
RenderExt could not project units / labels / digits.

Mirrors `spot/stop_double`'s `on_resume` (seed instrument → fetch
max-available) + `margin/mp`'s `on_visible` (spawn the shared
`pure_mp::session_watcher` SessionWatch effect):
1. Synchronously seed `state.instrument` from the session via the
shared `session_watcher::snapshot_from_session` (same mapping the
watcher uses) so `instId` is present BEFORE the fetch.
2. Dispatch `fetch_max_available` now that `instId` is non-empty
(margin path keeps `MaxAvailableManager::fetch_margin()`).
3. Spawn the persistent SessionWatch effect so the instrument +
ticker `last_price` stay live and re-seed on instrument switch,
re-fetching max-available on each switch.

name: refresh_trade_with_balances
doc:
Host is about to show the Trade-With picker — drop the cached balance
projection and re-fetch it.

Required for legacy parity: `TradeWithCryptoSelectDialog` fired
`fetchBalances()` from `onViewCreated`, i.e. on EVERY open, so the numbers were
never older than the current open. A cache that is only refreshed when the ccy
list changes would keep showing pre-trade / pre-transfer balances for the same
pair, and would not notice a login / logout / account switch either.

Clears first so the rows fall back to the "--" placeholder while the request is
in flight (also legacy behaviour), then commits whatever the manager returns.

name: update_instrument_snapshot
doc:
Apply a resolved spot instrument precision snapshot to the kernel.
Session projection and the standalone Rust biz-cache fallback both use
this writer. Without it the
internal `self.instrument` stays `None`, so `fetch_max_available`
renders "--" (max_avail stuck `Idle`) and `confirm_order` silently
returns (no order placed). Sibling parity:
`PureSpotLimitActions::update_instrument_snapshot`
(`../../limit/pure/spot_limit_interactor.rs:528`) +
`PureSpotAdvancedLimitActions::update_instrument_snapshot`.

Re-fires `fetch_max_available()` after binding so a snapshot that lands
after `start()` (the usual onResume race) still transitions the stuck
`Idle` max-avail into a real fetch.
